newsitem.title: USA: Valero sees 1997 capex on BASIS at $35 mln.
newsitem.headline: Valero sees 1997 capex on BASIS at $35 mln.

text.p: Valero Energy Corp will spend $37 million in 1997 to upgrade facilities at the three refineries that make up its $485 million BASIS purchase from Salomon Brothers, the company told a conference call Monday.
The company also said it would continue to look at other potential refinery acquisitions, but not until it had absorbed BASIS buy on May 1.
"We are talking about the BASIS buy being accretive to earnings almost immediately if we can get the right feedstock," said Bill Greehey, Valero's chairman and chief executive.
Greehy added that the company expected to firm up some 50 percent of BASIS feedstock on term agreements.

The three refineries being purchased have throughput of 300,000 barrels per day and Valero said that the refineries had generally been operating in excess of 95 percent of capacity during the past few years.
The buy brings Valero's total capacity to 500,000 barrels per day.
Valero said that it could reduce operating costs at the three refineries by $26 million a year and will run less residual product through the refinery.
Under the terms of the deal, Salomon is entitled to additional payments if the refining margins improve beyond a certain level up to $200 million total.
"We expect these payments will be $125 million over ten years," Valero's Greehy.
He added that the company was comfortable with analysts' forecasts of the low 30 cents earnings per share for Valero in the first quarter of 1997. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
